content.question_text: What are varargs methods in Java?

core_requirements: Methods that can accept a variable number of arguments.
The arguments are automatically wrapped into an array when the method is called.
acceptable_variations: Methods that can take zero or more arguments.

content.question_text: How do you denote in a method definition that a method can receive a variable number of parameters?

core_requirements: Using the ellipsis (...) after the parameter type.

content.question_text: How is a varargs method defined? Provide an example.
To what is Object... exactly the same at compile time?

acceptable_variations: It is compiled to an Object array.
The varargs parameter is treated as an array.

content.question_text: What happens if you pass a primitive type to a varargs method with parameter type Object...?

core_requirements: The primitive value is autoboxed to its corresponding wrapper class.
It is then passed as an Object array element.
acceptable_variations: Primitives get autoboxed to wrapper types.

content.question_text: Can you declare a varargs method with primitive type arguments (e.g., int...)?

core_requirements: The varargs syntax works with primitive types as well (int..., double..., etc.).
acceptable_variations: Yes, you can use int..., double..., etc.
